topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers

outline.topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers

sections.title: The Analogy: The 'Library' inside the Transformer
sections.content: Introduce the Transformer architecture components: Attention (the 'Reader' focusing on context) and MLPs (the 'Long-term Memory' storing fixed facts). Establish that MLPs act as key-value databases.
sections.example: Imagine a librarian (Attention) who reads a sentence, then consults a fixed encyclopedia (MLP) to look up obscure facts like 'The capital of France is Paris'.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Weight Vectors as Keys
sections.content: Explain that facts are encoded as weight matrices. A specific input (the 'query') activates a hidden layer neuron, which behaves like an address in memory. Visualizing weight vectors as directional arrows in high-dimensional space.
sections.example: Visualize a 'Key Vector' as a specific key-hole. When the concept 'France' passes through, it fits perfectly into the lock that holds the value 'Paris'.

sections.title: Mechanism: The Key-Value Memory Model
sections.content: Break down the MLP operation: Input x Weight_Matrix_1 (Key) -> Activation (Non-linearity) -> Weight_Matrix_2 (Value). Explain this as a 'Pattern Matching' process.
sections.example: A neuron acts like a light switch: if the input 'France' is detected, the switch turns ON, and it emits the stored 'Value' vector that points toward the concept 'Paris'.

sections.title: Visualizing Fact Storage: The Embedding Space
sections.content: Describe how training (gradient descent) shifts the weights to minimize error. Facts are 'etched' into the network by pulling the Value vector closer to the correct answer.
sections.example: Show a graph where a 'Concept Cloud' moves. Initially, 'France' is far from 'Paris'. After learning, the MLP weights are adjusted so the vector from 'France' points directly at the coordinate space representing 'Paris'.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
sections.content: Conclude that MLPs are not just calculators, but distributed storage systems. When we query the model, we are activating neurons that retrieve these 'etched' weights.
sections.example: Summary Animation: A neural network layer 'lighting up' in specific patterns to reconstruct the fact 'Paris' when given the input 'France', cementing the concept of neural memory.

storyboard.title: The Analogy: The 'Library' inside the Transformer
lecture_lines: Attention layers act as dynamic readers.
MLPs function as static, long-term memory.
Think of MLPs as a giant database.
They store facts like 'Paris is France's capital'.
